name.en: Tate-shiho-gatame escape by clamping and rolling

about.en: Being held astride is the hardest hold to escape and the most important to learn, because it is where a lock or a strangle usually follows. Clamping an arm and a leg on the same side removes their base on that side, and the bridge does the rest.

en: Clamp an arm and a leg on the same side, never opposite sides
Bridge high, then turn towards the clamped side
Keep your own elbows in so they cannot isolate an arm
You are held in Tate-shiho-gatame, your partner astride your waist with their knees tight to your sides.
Keep both of your elbows in against your ribs so neither arm can be isolated for a lock.
Trap one of their arms against your chest with both hands, thumb side up.
Bring your foot up on the same side and clamp their leg with your own, so their base on that side is gone.
Plant your other foot flat and bridge hard, driving your hips up and over the clamped side.
Turn into the clamped side as their weight tips and come out on top or in your guard. Release their arm as you arrive.

receiving.en: The instant an arm and a leg are clamped on the same side, you have no base there. Post your free hand wide on the mat past their head, sit up tall and take your weight off their chest before the bridge comes.

viNotes.en: Everything here is contact-based. The rule to remember is same side: the arm you clamp and the leg you clamp must be on the same side of your body, or the roll has somewhere to go. Feel for both before you bridge.
